thread:
jamie (support): heads-up — customer AcmeInc reporting ~15% 502s to hosted /v1/generate since 10:12:30 UTC. Started immediately after billing-header rotate. Short repro attached. trace ids: trx-8f3a, trx-8f3b
kevin (eng-sre): thx. can you paste the curl + full request headers and a sample trace-id from a failed request?
jamie (support): sure — sample curl:
```
curl -v -H 'Authorization: Bearer sk-xxxxx' -H 'X-Billing-Key: acct_123' \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -d '{"stream":true,"input":"hi"}'
```
failed response snippet:
```
HTTP/2 502
content-type: application/json
{ "error": "upstream_connection_reset", "trace": "trx-8f3a" }
```
jamie (support): headers include `x-redwood-billing-version: 2026-03-17T10:12:29Z` right before the spike. Also all failures were streaming requests (long-lived).
kevin (eng-sre): looking at edge logs now. I see repeated `upstream reset: connection failure` and `HTTP/2 RST_STREAM` around trx-8f3a. Does customer use any large prompt chunking or long sequences?
maria (eng-runtime): checking runtime metrics — auth-service latency spiked ~250ms at 10:12:30 for a short window, and auth-cache shows a batch eviction at 10:12:29. When cache evicts, we see auth lookups hit auth-service sync path which can briefly push upstream queues.
kevin (eng-sre): that matches. Hypothesis: billing-header rotate triggers auth-cache version bump -> eviction -> auth-service synchronous calls increase -> upstream keeps connections for streaming requests but auth latency causes edge to hit upstream timeout and return 502. Might be H2 window/connection stall + eviction flood.
sophie (eng-platform): we did a config push for the billing header rollout at 10:12:30 across regions (flag flip + header schema). I'll pause the rollout for remaining regions and roll back the last batch in us-west-2.
tyler (support): customer is on reserved capacity (dedicated) but this call was to hosted api. I offered them to switch to dedicated routing temporarily; they prefer a fix. I've told them we are investigating and to expect an update in ~30m.
kevin (eng-sre): quick mitigation experiment: increase auth-cache soft TTL to 60s and edge upstream idle timeout -> 35s to avoid mid-stream upstream resets. Also enabling a short fallback path that allows requests to proceed with cached anon token when auth latency high. I'll open a change.
maria (eng-runtime): I can reproduce locally by forcing auth-cache eviction and streaming a request with `--stream` for 30s. Repro script:
```
# repro: force eviction, then start streaming request
python tools/evict_auth_cache.py --target=acct_123 && \
curl -H 'Authorization: Bearer sk-xxxxx' -H 'X-Billing-Key: acct_123' https://staging.api.redwood.ai/v1/generate?stream=true
```
Log shows: `envoy upstream error: stream reset, code=ENHANCE_YOUR_CALM` then 502 at the edge.
kevin (eng-sre): deployed a quick rollback for the billing-header config in us-west-2 — deploy id rollback-2026-03-17-10:18:40. deploy-bot: kicked.
deploy-bot: Rollback started for config billing-header-rollout (id: rollback-2026-03-17-10:18:40)
kevin (eng-sre): after rollback start, error rate dropped back to baseline within ~20s. Still want permanent fix: make auth-cache eviction staggered + add an edge-side graceful auth path for streaming (avoid synchronous auth handshake per chunk).
sophie (eng-platform): agree — we'll change rollout to staged background evictions and add telemetry tags `auth_cache_hit`, `billing_header_version` to traces.
tyler (support): customer updated: they saw errors drop after a minute and appreciate the update. Keeping them informed.
maria (eng-runtime): follow-ups: add unit test for streaming + cache eviction, add synthetic that simulates header rotate during load. I'll file a bug.
jeff (jamie) (support): noted, I'll keep thread open until fixes land and customer confirms. Thanks all.
